factProposals.value: A file is treated as parsed tabular rows (header-keyed, like csv.DictReader output), not raw bytes -- PHI detection runs on column headers and cell values after parsing, not on the file's binary content.

PHI detection is two-layered: a deterministic column-header match against known patient-name/birth-date/record-number field names, plus a content-based fallback that catches an SSN-shaped value even under an unrelated header.

The audit entry logged for a rejected file never carries the PHI value itself -- only the offending column name and category. Verified directly: the raw value is asserted absent from the logged entry's string representation, not just assumed absent.

decisions.statement: Built a gate function (ingest_file_with_phi_gate) around injected store/log_audit callables, rather than only a scan/detector function, so that 'reject before storage' and 'reject before logging' are enforced by construction and are genuinely testable now.
decisions.rationale: STORY-005 (operator uploads) does not exist yet, so there is no real storage or logging call to wrap. STORY-011's grounding_guardrail.py was built as a standalone detector the same way and its story stayed unticked because nothing calls it -- ticking STORY-010 off a detector alone would repeat that gap. Injecting store/log_audit lets the actual gating behavior (store never runs on a rejected file; log_audit never receives row content) be proven with unit tests today, and STORY-005 supplies the real Supabase write and logger later without this function changing.

decisions.statement: SSN-shaped content (\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}) is classified under the 'record_number' category, extending REQ-009's three named categories (names, birth dates, record numbers) rather than adding a fourth.
decisions.rationale: REQ-009 does not name SSN explicitly, but a government identifier tied to a patient functions as exactly the kind of record number the requirement means to keep out; folding it into the existing category avoided widening the requirement's scope.

limitations.statement: Detection of patient names and birth dates is header-based only; there is no content-based fallback for these two categories the way there is for record numbers (SSN pattern). A patient name under a generic header like 'value', or a birth date under a header that doesn't say DOB, would not be caught. Generic content matching was deliberately not attempted: free text can't be reliably classified as 'a name' without a model, and financial exports carry legitimate business dates (report date, posting date) that a naive date-shape check would false-positive on.

The gate (ingest_file_with_phi_gate) is exercised only against injected test doubles for store/log_audit, since the real Supabase write and the real logger (STORY-005) do not exist in this repo yet. The gating logic is proven; the real side effects it will eventually wrap are not.

demonstrationEvidence.ref: pipeline/test_phi_guardrail.py (22 tests: header-based detection for all three REQ-009 categories, SSN-content fallback, false-positive avoidance on business dates, and the ingest gate proving rejection happens before storage and before the PHI value ever reaches a log); full pipeline/ suite (52 tests total) run clean with no regressions
